Foreknowledge is a short allowlist. A catalog of “what each of 204 is good for” is how the $20 dies.

Cursor bills **two pools**, not one tank. **Cursor Models** (generous, included): Cursor Grok 4.6/4.5 and Composer 2.5. **Other Models** ($20/mo on Pro, then on-demand at API rates): Claude, GPT, Gemini, Kimi, GLM. Composer Fast is a **speed surcharge** ($3/$15 vs $0.50/$2.50), not a cheaper SKU — and Cursor’s own default. Composer 2.5 is built on Moonshot **Kimi K2.5**. Kimi K3 on Other Models is **$3/$15** — Sonnet rates, not a bargain.

“Efficient Kimi K3” is efficient versus Opus-through-Cursor, not versus Codex/Grok/Gemini at $0. That rationalization is the spend engine.

---

## 1. The trigger rule

Reach for the bench only when **one named trigger fires**, then still pass the pool gate. Log the trigger name on the spend row.

**T1 · ALIEN_LINEAGE.** The job needs a producing vendor not in `{anthropic, openai, xai, google}`. Today that is Moonshot (Composer / Kimi) or Zhipu/Z.ai (GLM). Default door: `composer-2.5` on Cursor Models. Other Models (`kimi-*`, `glm-*`) only after consent in §2.

**T2 · HOUSE_TRANSPORT_DEAD.** Preflight: the needed house seat is UNREACHABLE **and** the Gemini Overflow Valve cannot cover **and** the lane would otherwise halt. A Cursor-hosted **mirror** of that vendor may **build**, never **review** that lineage’s work. Prefer Cursor Models (Cursor Grok, Composer) over Other Models clones.

**T3 · BOSS_NAMED.** the operator named the family or slug.

**T4 · PROVEN_DELTA.** The shop lineage ledger (Doctrine 6) has ≥3 objective rows where this family beat the house alternative on this task type, **and** the weekly review adopted the route. Until then: suggest only.

**T5 · ALIEN_CONTEXT.** The artifact will not fit a house window **and** the only fit is an alien 1M (today: `kimi-k3-*`). Never Cursor-hosted Claude/GPT/Fable 1M — that is T2-or-nothing, and T2 prefers the house overflow valve.

**Pool gate (not a trigger):** if the candidate burns Other Models while a house seat of the same lineage is up, the trigger is void. Cheap versus $0 is not cheaper. “Cost/volume shape” is **not** a trigger in this shop. “It’s on the Cursor Models pool so it’s free” is also not a trigger — generous ≠ infinite, and the house twin is still $0.

**Wrong — do not reach**

- **W1 MIRROR_SPEND** — house seat for that lineage is up. Cursor-Claude / GPT / Grok / Gemini are parked.
- **W2 INDEPENDENCE_LAUNDER** — Cursor-hosted brain reviewing its own vendor’s house work.
- **W3 VOLUME / “try a few”** — a 3-model bench sample is an unasked fleet.
- **W4 FAST_MEANS_CHEAP** — `-fast` is a surcharge (Composer Fast is 6×; Cursor Grok Fast is 2×).
- **W5 OVERFLOW_THEFT** — Claude meter hot → Gemini Overflow Valve (flat Google tab), never Cursor.
- **W6 MECHANICAL** — sweeps, docs polish, log mines: Gemini Flash at $0.
- **W7 CURIOSITY** — “see how K3 does” is not T4.
- **W8 ON_DEMAND or UNKNOWN POOL** — treat as bench DEAD.
- **W9 PLANNING** — host Claude already plans. Cursor Opus/Fable 1M thinking is the fastest way to empty Other Models.
- **W10 AUTO / UNKNOWN LINEAGE** — `auto` and unmapped slugs fail closed for review.
- **W11 REPLACE_GROK** — Cursor Grok while house Grok answers. Same job, worse bill, illegal as my reviewer. Included-pool is not a license to recast Appendix A.

**Rule text:** *House first. Bench only on T1–T5. Mirrors parked. Fast is not cheap. Overflow is green, not Cursor. Included is not free.*

---

## 2. Suggest vs. summon

Spend is irreversible. A standing permit is a **PLAN-CARD field the boss writes**. The orchestrator may not grant itself one.

| Act | Allowed |
|---|---|
| **Silent summon** (announce the wrap, do not wait) | Only with a standing permit: `composer-2.5` (**not** `-fast`), purpose named in the permit, daily cap not hit, Cursor Models pool, fresh call, files in the repo before the call ends |
| **Suggest** (one line, wait) | Default. Any Other Models family. First use of a family. T4 not met. the operator’s “long Kimi review.” Any `-fast`. Effort `max`/`xhigh`. T5. |
| **Explicit ruling** | On-demand. Any `claude-*` / `gpt-*` / `gemini-*` through Cursor. Bench as sole builder of a write-set. Bench in a council. Cursor Grok while house Grok is up. Changing the wrapper default. |
| **Hard refuse — do not even offer** | On-demand as a continuation path. W1–W11. `auto` as a reviewer. Reply-chain dressed as a review. “House was slow so I used Fast.” |

**Suggest line:** *“Bench T1: Moonshot eyes on this Claude-built review. Cheap door: `composer-2.5` on Cursor Models. Expensive door: `kimi-k3-high` on Other Models (API $3/$15 — Sonnet rates). House alternative: Codex. Permit: none. Spin which, or neither?”*

Silent summon still narrates. Hide the spend and it is theft: `♾️ composer-2.5 reviewing parser ♾️` or `💸 kimi-k3-high 💸`. Cursor Models = ♾️ wrap. Other Models = 💸 wrap. On-demand (forbidden) would be 🚨💳.

Cursor Grok is **never** silently summoned while house Grok answers.

Preflight of the **transport** (`wmw-cursor` Connected) is not a summon. Probing 204 models is.

---

## 3. The ledger’s shape

**~9 rows, not 204.** Effort tiers are a column, not a row. `-fast` is a boolean surcharge, not a model. File: `cursor-bench-ledger.md` next to the dispatch guide. This is a **capability catalog**, not Doctrine 6’s outcome ledger — do not merge them.

**Table A — MIRRORS (parked). Four rows, not 195 SKUs.**

| family | lineage | house | pool | independence | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-*` | anthropic | 🟠 | other-models | FORBIDDEN vs Claude | PARKED |
| `gpt-*` | openai | 🔵 | other-models | FORBIDDEN vs Codex | PARKED |
| `cursor-grok-*` | xai (Cursor+xAI joint) | ⚫ | cursor-models | FORBIDDEN vs Grok | LIMP-HOME-ONLY |
| `gemini-*` | google | 🟢 | other-models | FORBIDDEN vs Gemini | PARKED |

**Table B — ALIENS (the actual catalog). Five rows.**

One row each: `composer-2.5` · `kimi-k3-high` · `kimi-k2.7-code` · `glm-5.2` · `glm-5.2-max`.

Columns:

`slug` · `family` · `lineage_vendor` (**Composer = moonshot**, not a unique Cursor vendor) · `pool` (`cursor-models` \| `other-models`) · `default_effort` (`high`, never `max` by default) · `fast` (`false`) · `may_review` · `must_not_review` (Composer ↛ Kimi ↛ Composer) · `job_fit` (one line, or empty) · `permit_class` (`silent` \| `suggest` \| `ruling`) · `last_live_probe` (ISO date) · `last_dispatch` · `proven_for` · `status` (`LIVE` / `STALE` / `DEAD`)

No dollar amounts in the catalog. Pool membership and `fast` are the money facts that survive a price change. Live rates live on the vendor page (SPINE currency rule).

**Anti-rot.** `proven_for` stays **EMPTY** until T4. Empty is honest; a paragraph of unverified “good for” is fiction. Probe older than 14 days → `STALE` → cannot auto-summon. Unknown slug → not a row → UNKNOWN LINEAGE. `cursor-agent models` refreshes **membership**, never flavor.

**Who updates.** Orchestrator pings Table B on preflight (LIVE/DEAD for the session). After a real dispatch: one Doctrine-6 lineage row. Weekly lineage review: only then may `proven_for` or `permit_class` change, and **the boss rules each change**.

No per-model emojis. SPINE retired 🟣. Cursor is a transport. Banner is lineage color + meter wrap.

---

## 4. What the bench is genuinely good for

**Very little.** Four house lineages already cover planning → building → reviewing → post-project. The only honest surplus is a **5th gene pool**, and even that has a cheap door.

| Phase | Call | Slug | Why not house |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Planning** | **Never** | — | Host Claude plans. Cursor Opus/Fable 1M thinking is Other Models at frontier API rates. One pass can empty the $20. Fable 5 is ~$10/$50. |
| **Building** | Rare | `composer-2.5` (non-fast) | 5th builder on a boss-widened ticket, or T2 when house builders are down. Default builder stays Codex. `glm-5.2` = suggest-only. Never Cursor GPT/Claude to build. Write-capable + metered = the pool’s fastest leak. |
| **Reviewing** | **The only real job** | Cheap door: `composer-2.5`. Money-smart alien: `glm-5.2` (Zhipu — can review Composer; API $1.4/$4.4). Capability-max alien: `kimi-k3-high` (not max, not fast) when the job actually needs K3, not K2.5 | House already has Codex (sharpest code), Claude (architecture), Gemini (cheap 4th). Bench is the **5th** read, not the 1st. |
| **Post-project** | Almost never | `composer-2.5` suggest-only for an alien retro | Sweeps/docs: Gemini Flash at $0. |

**Against my own interest:** do not send code reviews to house Grok to keep me employed — Codex already owns that. Do not block a 5th-lineage review. If Composer or GLM proves more catches than I do on a task type, T4 should move that work off me. **Do** block Cursor Grok as a Grok replacement: same family, metered transport, illegal as my reviewer, and the “included pool” story is how I get silently cloned.

Andrew’s Kimi example: allow as **suggest**, not as the default “efficient” path. The efficient Moonshot review is Composer on Cursor Models. Kimi K3 is the upgrade that spends Other Models at Sonnet rates, and it cannot independently review Composer.

Speed (Composer Fast, 4.7s) is real and is **not a trigger**. House Gemini Flash is $0. Pay 6× only when the boss names latency.

---

## 5. Lineage safety

Cursor is a **host**, never a vendor. Independence compares `lineage_vendor`. Giving the host a fifth color is how Claude-on-Cursor becomes “a different seat” in the orchestrator’s head.

| slug prefix | lineage |
|---|---|
| `claude-` | anthropic |
| `gpt-` | openai |
| `cursor-grok-` | xai |
| `gemini-` | google |
| `kimi-` / `composer-` | **moonshot** |
| `glm-` | zhipu |
| `auto` / unmapped | UNKNOWN |

**Mechanism**

1. Every review ticket carries `builder_lineage`. Catalog match → refuse as `FULL CROSS-VENDOR`. Boss-launched same-vendor is `SOLO-VENDOR DEGRADED` and must be labeled.
2. Composer and Kimi cannot review each other. GLM can review both.
3. Banner never lies: `🟠💸 claude-sonnet-5 on Cursor`, not “🟣 Cursor.” Narrate `composer-2.5 (moonshot) reviewing 🟠 Claude`.
4. Unmapped slug = UNKNOWN LINEAGE = cannot count. `auto` banned on review tickets (the router hides the brain).
5. Arsenal line: *“House online: 🟠 Claude · 🔵 Codex · ⚫ Grok · 🟢 Gemini. Bench: RESERVE (Composer/Kimi/GLM) · mirrors PARKED.”* Do not list Cursor as a fifth house color.
6. Wrapper-level (preferred, because habits die): `wmw-cursor` review path requires `builder_lineage`; reject on match; reject `auto`; default model `composer-2.5` **not** `-fast`. Today’s default is already the surcharge sitting in the gun.
7. A Cursor session that built, edited, or was briefed on the work is in that work’s owning-seat lineage forever (Transport Law #3). Fresh call is necessary, not sufficient.

---

## 6. The budget rule

Subscription-only survives if **on-demand is illegal** and Other Models is an accident budget, not an allocation. The orchestrator cannot read remaining pool (SPINE honesty limit) — so it cannot “spend until empty.” It uses a **declared cap**.

```
cursor_bench:                    # PLAN-CARD, boss-owned
  status: RESERVE                # not a house seat
  on_demand: FORBIDDEN
  other_models: included-only    # $20 then STOP
  expected_other_models_spend: $0
  standing_permit: []            # boss fills; empty = suggest-only
  daily_other_models_cap: 0      # auto-summon of Other Models = none
  daily_cursor_models_cap: 3     # even the "included" pool is capped
  default_slug: composer-2.5     # NOT composer-2.5-fast
  fast_variants: ask
```

Spend ledger (jsonl, one row per call): `date · slug · pool · trigger · purpose · session_id · tokens`. Read it before every summon. The wrapper already prints tokens in the footer — log them.

**Pool empty or plan lapses:** bench = `DEAD`. LIMP HOME on house seats. Do not retry. Do not promise “finish on Cursor tomorrow.” Do not enable on-demand. Cursor’s own docs offer on-demand or an upgrade at the cap — this shop picks **neither** at dispatch time. Upgrade is a boss ruling outside the run.

**What actually breaks on lapse:** reply-chains die; `sessionId` goes invalid; an in-flight review vanishes; the orchestrator “helpfully” retries on-demand. Counter: bench work lands in the **repo** before the call returns (Principle 4 — files are the shared brain). Sessions are smoke. The bench must never be the sole builder of a write-set — a house seat must be able to finish the lane. If the bench dies mid-review, that review is incomplete; fall back to a house reviewer. Do not pause the mission for a metered seat.

**The included-pool launder:** “Cursor Grok / Composer is on Cursor Models, so summon freely” is how a $20 shop burns the generous tank, then treats empty as permission to open Other Models, then treats empty Other Models as permission to go on-demand. Each step sounds cheap. Cap both pools. Expected monthly Other Models spend ≈ $0. If the weekly lineage review shows Other Models spend without a T1/T3/T5 row, that is abuse, flagged to the boss.

---

## 7. One thing I would refuse to build

**The Model Mall: a 204-row catalog plus a silent fit-router.**

That object is the abuse engine. It invites unasked fleets. It goes stale in a week. It trains the orchestrator to spend. It hides `-fast` as a default. It makes `wmw-cursor` look like a fifth vendor so Cursor-Claude can “independently” review Claude. It is the method’s original scar — *an unfenced instance spawning a swarm and torching a day of frontier budget* — with a SKU list and a credit card attached.

The wrapper’s current default `composer-2.5-fast` is already that mall’s first product on the shelf.

Also refuse, for the same reason:

- On-demand as a continuation path (the subscription-only doctrine dies here, not in a manifesto).
- Cataloging the 195 mirror SKUs as dispatchable tools.
- Resurrecting 🟣 as Cursor’s color (SPINE v4.0 retired it; a host is not a lineage).
- Using this seat as a Claude overflow valve (that job is already Gemini/agy, on a flat tab).
- A house-to-bench failover (“Grok was slow, so Cursor Grok”). That is how I get replaced by a metered clone of myself, and the independence channel lies about it.

Foreknowledge is Table B (five slugs) plus Table A (four parked globs). Anything larger is costume.

---

**If you only adopt one thing, adopt this**

The bench is a **reserve of two alien lineages**, not a 204-model house seat. Default door is `composer-2.5` (non-fast, Cursor Models, Moonshot). Other Models (Kimi/GLM/any mirror) is suggest-only, on-demand is illegal, and Cursor-hosted Claude/GPT/Grok/Gemini never count as independent of their house twins.

House first. Mirrors parked. Fast is not cheap. Included is not free. The catalog that stays true is nine rows with empty `proven_for` until the ledger earns a sentence.

   - The task is a long-running code sweep or post-project retrospective where house seats would 100 % hit rate limits.

   - The task is a Composer-family codegen step where the wrapper default is Composer 2.5-fast and the house seats cannot match the token budget.
